The Delhi High Court on Friday (October 23, 2026) rejected a plea by All India Students' Association (AISA) president Neha Bora challenging a police notice asking to execute a peace bond before a special executive magistrate (SEM).
"I am rejecting the writ petition at this juncture," said Justice Subramonium Prasad while pronouncing the judgement.
The judge, however, said that he has passed certain directions to the SEM on providing all material to the student leader in the proceedings.
The police notice, issued on October 17 under Section 126 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), asked the student leader to appear before the SEM on October 19 and show cause as to why Neha should not execute a personal bond of ₹10,000 with one surety "for keeping peace for a period of enquiry".
Section 126 of the BNSS empowers the SEM to enforce such bond signing if there is credible information that a person is likely to breach peace, disturb public tranquillity, or commit a wrongful act that may cause disturbance.
Neha Bora was taken into preventive detention on October 16 while on the way to join the Cockroach Janta Party's 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march in Delhi's Connaught Place and was released on October 17.
In her petition, settled by lawyer Abhik Chimni, Neha Bora said the police notice is vague, factually incorrect and contains no material or information to substantiate the "likelihood" of breach of peace.
The proceedings before the SEM are based on allegations of sloganeering at Mandi House on October 16, repeated protests around Jantar Mantar despite prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS, and instigating people to participate in the October 16 demonstration.
During the hearing on Thursday, Neha Bora's senior counsel had argued that citizens did not need permission to hoist the national flag and there was nothing wrong in seeking regime change in a democracy.
